Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move from pilot to production. Before we spin up Dedicated capacity we need a short, pragmatic handover from Redwood on the observability side so our SREs can take ownership. Key asks from our side: 

- A compact runbook for common incidents (token errors, KV cache evictions, degraded throughput)
- Dashboard templates for per-route latency, token cost, and error taxonomy counts
- Tracing hook examples so we can correlate requests in our trace collector
- Alert routing suggestions by severity and suggested on-call roles

I've attached a brief scope doc (aurora_visibility_scope.pdf) and cc'd our eng inbox. Can we get a 30–45m working session next week to align owners and deliverables? Ideally we'd have an initial draft runbook and dashboards within two weeks.

Appreciate the help — Elena

- Alert routing (owner: Soojin Lee): recommended severity mapping + on-call role mapping + sample PagerDuty entries.

Proposed timeline: kickoff next Tue (2026-09-15) 10:00–10:45 PT, internal owners will produce first-draft artifacts by 2026-09-22. If that works I will send a calendar invite and a shared Drive folder with templates.

Hi all,

Adding a couple of pragmatic items to smooth the implementation: 

1) Error taxonomy: I'll produce a one-page mapping that groups errors into three buckets for Aurora: 
   - Transient (rate limit, short-lived infra glitches) — auto-retry guidance (backoff + jitter)
   - Recoverable (model timeout, tokenization mismatch) — mitigation steps + fallback models
   - Critical (auth failures, data-corruption signals) — immediate paging + service quarantine note

2) Tracing hooks: Ben and I recommend the following span pattern: 
   - root span: "aurora.request" with tags {route_id, customer_id, model_variant} 
   - child spans for "tokenize", "inference", "post_process" — include per-span token counts and latency_ms
   We'll include example code snippets in both Node and Flask.

3) Dashboard cadence: Laura will upload views for a 1-hour, 6-hour and 24-hour lookback. For cost-sensitive routes we suggest adding token-cost alerts when 24h moving average > baseline * 1.5.

Scheduling: confirming Soojin's Tue 10am PT works for me. If Aurora can send SRE names + a read-only sample key by EOD Monday, Ben will validate trace ingestion before the call.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Customer Success — Observability
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick clarifications from the dashboard and ops side before the kickoff:

- Access: please provide a project-level read-only API key and one sample trace id (or a synthetic trace file) so I can validate the dashboard import and trace correlation queries.
- Alert routing note: we suggest mapping "Critical" -> immediate page to on-call (PagerDuty service: aurora-inference-critical), "High" -> Slack @aurora-sre and email to secondary on-call, "Medium/Low" -> Slack digest. I will include a sample PD config export in the Drive.
- Runbook format: PDF + markdown in the Drive. We'll keep the PDF short (1–2 pages per incident) and a single canonical markdown repo for edits.

I'll prepare the dashboard JSON for 1hr/6hr/24hr and a short playbook template before the call. Will also add a visualization for "error taxonomy counts by service" that breaks down the buckets Marissa mentioned.
